thread:
support-eng: FYI - multiple customers reporting 503s on hosted inference since 18:34 UTC. Saw upstream runner restart loop on nodes in us-west-2.

support-eng: Root logs show a SIGILL / illegal instruction from the model process right before the container OOM/restart sequence. Suspect a CUDA/cudnn mismatch or a bad kernel after a recent model swap.

maria.g: Which model(s) and which commit/version did the swap? Any pattern in input size or batch size?

support-eng: Affected model: gptx-small-quant (quantized variant). Swap occurred at 18:33:49 to commit f2a3b1. Most requests are short (<512 tokens) but we saw a spike in batched requests (batch_size=16) around 18:34:10 from internal load test.

devon: Logs pasted:
```
[18:34:12] infer-runner[pid=2419]: runtime error: illegal instruction (SIGILL)
[18:34:12] kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
[18:34:12] docker: container exited with code 132
[18:34:13] kubelet: eviction: restarting container infer-runner x3 in 30s
```

kai: container exit code 132 -> SIGILL. Could be JITed kernel or a PTX incompatibility with the driver. Any driver churn or node OS updates rolled recently?

lina: No infra updates in us-west-2 last 24h. We did roll a new model artifact that switches to a fused attention kernel variant for int8 perf.

devon: That matches - fused kernel may emit instructions not supported on older GPU microcode or mismatched CUDA. Check `nvidia-smi -q` and `dmesg` on the host that saw the failure.

support-eng: Pulled host diagnostics from node id node-uw2-013: `nvidia-smi` shows Driver 525.85, CUDA 12.1. dmesg has repeated `NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus` entries starting 18:34:12.

maria.g: Customer impact? Which tenants routed to those nodes?

support-eng: Two customers: acme-analytics (high QPS embedding jobs) and voxchat. We're seeing increased 503s for both, more severe for voxchat since they use streaming. CS has been looped in.

kai: Quick mitigations: 1) Remove the fused-attn flag from the model runtime and redeploy the previous artifact. 2) Temporarily drain the affected nodes and route traffic to fallback pool (cpu/fallback-gpu). 3) Enable per-request fallback to older model variant.

lina: Pushing a rollback now (reverting to f1b2c3 artifact) and initiating draining. ETA 5m.

ops-bot: @support-eng triggered route-fallback policy for acme-analytics -> fallback-gpu (policy id: rf-331).

support-eng: After rollback, initial observations: runner stays up, no SIGILL seen in first 90s. However we still saw one OOM entry during a large batched embed job: `OOM when allocating tensor with shape [16, 2048, 4096]` at 18:41.

devon: That suggests two separate failure modes: (1) illegal instruction from new fused kernel on certain GPU/driver combos; (2) genuine memory pressure from unexpectedly large batch shapes. Both cause 503s via upstream worker death.

maria.g: Repro steps for ENG to validate:
1) Spin up a runner on a node with driver 525.85 / CUDA12.1.
2) Deploy artifact f2a3b1 with fused-attn flag.
3) Send mixed QPS load with short chitchat requests + periodic batch embeddings (batch_size 16, seq_len 2048).
4) Watch dmesg and container exit codes.

kai: Also try on node with driver 520.x to see if failure is driver-specific. Capture the `cuobjdump` / kernel arch flags from the artifact.

support-eng: CS update sent to customers: "We're investigating upstream runner crashes causing transient 503s. We've initiated rollback and fallback routing; your traffic is being served from alternate capacity. We'll follow up with a postmortem."

lina: Rolling metrics: 503 rate for acme-analytics down from 7.2% -> 0.4% after routing. Voxchat still at ~2% due to streaming; investigating their longest running requests.

devon: Long-term fixes: - Prevent fused kernel being selected for artifacts unless `min_driver_version` metadata satisfied. - Add pre-deploy smoke tests that run quick kernel compatibility checks on representative node images. - Improve autoscaling to avoid huge batch windows landing on single runner.

maria.g: Who's owning the postmortem? Recommend eng-runtime + eng-ml + eng-sre.

support-eng: I'll own initial incident write-up. tagging @devon @kai @lina for follow-ups.

ops-bot: Incident #INC-3605001234 opened and assigned to support-eng.

kai: Quick note for CS and billing: mark affected requests as retried so customers don't get double-billed; we'll confirm once logs are reconciled.

lina: Action items created:
- rollback confirmation (lina)
- node drain + forensic logs (sre)
- reproduce with driver matrix (eng-ml)
- postmortem (support-eng)

support-eng: Will update thread with postmortem link when ready. Thanks all :thumbsup:"
